body:
`pep508_rs` 0.9.2 (latest on crates.io) panics instead of returning `Err(Pep508Error)` when a requirement's name ends in `-` and is followed by further input (specifier, extras, URL, marker, whitespace).

## Reproducer

```toml
[dependencies]
pep508_rs = "=0.9.2"
```

```rust
use std::str::FromStr;

fn main() {
    let _ = pep508_rs::Requirement::<pep508_rs::VerbatimUrl>::from_str("D-==1");
}
```

Output:

```
`PackageName` validation should match PEP 508 parsing: InvalidNameError("D-")
```

## Observed

Panics (same message, name varies): `"D-==1"`, `"D->=1"`, `"D- >=1"`, `"D-[x]"`, `"D-("`, `"D-@https://x/y"`, `"D-; python_version>'3'"`, `"foo-[bar]>=1.0"`, trailing tab `"D-\t"`.

Returns a normal `Err` (expected behavior): `"D-"` alone, `"a-"`, `"a_"`, `"a."`, `"-a"`, `"foo--"`.

## Expected

An `Err(Pep508Error)` such as the one produced for `"D-"` alone: `Package name must end with an alphanumeric character, not '-'`.

## Cause

The tokenizer accepts the name token, then re-validates it via `PackageName` and `.expect()`s success, but `PackageName` validation rejects a trailing `-` that the tokenizer accepted. The two checks disagree. This is reachable from untrusted input (e.g. a `requirements.txt` line), so a parser embedded in a long-running process (such as a language server) has to wrap it in `catch_unwind`, and libfuzzer targets abort on it.
title: pep508_rs 0.9.2: Requirement::from_str panics on a package name ending in '-' followed by more input
